plan.title: Attention Is All You Need
plan.coverPrompt: A clean whiteboard sketch of a grid of words connected by lines of different thickness, showing which words attend to which, in a calm educational style

steps.title: Queries, keys and values
steps.goal: Each token's vector is multiplied by three learned weight matrices to give its query, its key and its value. Show the three projections on a small example.

steps.title: Scaled dot-product scores
steps.goal: Scaled dot-product attention: multiply Q by K transpose to get the scores, then divide by the square root of d_k. Work a small numeric example.

steps.title: Softmax over the scores
steps.goal: Softmax over the attention scores: turn one row of scores into weights that sum to one, then use them to mix the rows of V.

steps.title: Multi-head attention
steps.goal: Multi-head attention: several heads attend in parallel with their own projections, then their outputs are concatenated and projected.

steps.title: Positional encoding
steps.goal: Attention alone ignores word order, so the paper adds sine and cosine positional encodings of different frequencies to the embeddings. Show the values for a few positions and dimensions.

plan.title: Newton's Method in Three Precisions
plan.coverPrompt: A clean whiteboard sketch of a curve with tangent lines stepping down to its root, drawn in three ink colours, in a calm educational style

steps.title: The Newton step
steps.goal: The Newton iteration x+ = xc - F'(xc)^-1 F(xc): solve the Jacobian system for the step, then update. Work one step on a small 2x2 system.

steps.title: Iterative refinement
steps.goal: Iterative refinement: solve with a cheap low-precision factorization, compute the residual in higher precision, and correct, repeating until the residual is small.

steps.title: Why three precisions
steps.goal: Why three precisions: residual in double, Jacobian stored in single, factorization in half, because the O(N^3) factorization dominates the cost.

steps.title: How fast it converges
steps.goal: What the paper's analysis says about how fast the iteration converges when the Jacobian and its factorization are kept in lower precision than the residual.

steps.title: What the experiments show
steps.goal: The paper's numerical results: compare the iteration histories of the precision combinations it tests, and what they show about cost and accuracy.
